title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to -90.0, 0.0, -90.0 and a translation vector of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0. Begin by drawing a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, draw the first loop consisting of four lines: the first line starts at (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0168, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.0168, 0.0) and ends at (0.0168, 0.0561); the third line starts at (0.0168, 0.0561) and ends at (0.0, 0.0561); and the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0561) and ends at (0.0, 0.0). Apply a sketch scale of 0.0561 to the two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the specified Euler angles and translate it using the specified translation vector. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to generate the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction, creating a new solid body. The resulting shape is a cylindrical object with a flat rectangular section at one end, measuring 0.01683291770573566 meters in length, 0.05610972568578553 meters in width, and 0.75 meters in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0168, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0168, 0.0561) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0561) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The given Euler angles are -90.0, 0.0, -90.0 and the translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
# This transformation can be achieved by rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
